newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Won's fall vs dollar "too sharp" - BOK official.
newsitem.headline: Won's fall vs dollar "too sharp" - BOK official.

text.p: The depreciation of the won against the dollar on the interbank market was "too sharp" and undesirable, a senior central Bank of Korea (BOK) official said on Monday.
The won touched an 84-month low of 879.70 against the U.S. unit during the morning session after opening at 876.70.
"The recent rise in the dollar/won rate has been too sharp and is not desirable for South Korea's economy," the senior BOK official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters by telephone.
"Particularly in light of the dollar's steadiness against the yen today, the dollar seems to be rising too quickly against the won," he added.
The dollar drifted near 124.60 yen in quiet mid-morning trading in Tokyo.
The official said many major corporations had expressed concern over foreign exchange losses triggered by the won's depreciation.
"Besides this, steep rises in the dollar will stimulate inflation, which is not at all desirable for our economy," he added. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5644
